en.title: Brad Bird's 'Ray Gunn' Finally Lands December 2026 Netflix Release Date
en.summary: After nearly three decades in development, legendary director Brad Bird's sci-fi noir passion project, Ray Gunn, has an official Netflix premiere date. The highly anticipated animated feature will debut globally in late 2026.
en.body:
The wait is almost over for animation aficionados. **Brad Bird**’s ambitious sci-fi noir detective story, **Ray Gunn**, has officially locked in its global premiere for December 18, 2026, exclusively on Netflix. This marks the culmination of a project that has been gestating for nearly 30 years, a testament to Bird's unwavering dedication to bringing his unique vision to life.

The journey of **Ray Gunn** began in 1996 when Bird and **Matthew Robbins** first penned the script. Initially envisioned as a 2D hand-drawn animated film and developed at Turner Animation, the project struggled for years to find a studio willing to commit to its grand scale and slightly more mature thematic elements. Bird himself revealed at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival that the initial spark for the film came from a delightful mishearing of the B-52s track "Planet Claire," which sounded to him like Henry Mancini's iconic "Peter Gunn" theme, leading to the project's distinctive title.

## A Star-Studded Sci-Fi Noir

While details have been scarce for years, the recent Netflix showcase at Annecy provided the first substantial look at the film. **Ray Gunn** is set to be a visually stunning dive into a retro-futuristic world, blending the moody aesthetics of noir with imaginative science fiction. The film is part of the multi-year deal between Netflix and Skydance Animation, and it will serve as the third feature to emerge from this collaboration.

The voice cast alone is enough to generate significant buzz. Leading the charge are **Sam Rockwell**, **Scarlett Johansson**, and the legendary **Tom Waits**. Their involvement promises nuanced performances that will breathe life into Bird's meticulously crafted characters and complex narrative. The film's runtime has also been confirmed at a crisp 1 hour and 59 minutes, a length that should allow for a compelling and tightly paced story.

## The Long Road to December 2026

For fans who have followed the whispers and rumors surrounding **Ray Gunn** for decades, this official release date is monumental. It signifies not just the arrival of a new animated film, but the triumphant realization of a director's long-held dream. The anticipation is palpable, especially given Bird's track record with beloved films like *The Iron Giant*, *The Incredibles*, and *Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse* (which he produced).

The film's premiere at the London Film Festival will likely offer a deeper dive into its narrative and artistic choices, providing critics and audiences alike with the first official reviews. The animated feature is poised to be a significant entry in Netflix's growing library of original animated content, aiming to captivate both seasoned animation enthusiasts and general audiences with its unique blend of genre and directorial flair.

## What's Next

With the December 18, 2026 release date firmly established, all eyes will be on Netflix and Skydance Animation for further glimpses, trailers, and promotional materials in the lead-up to the premiere. Fans can expect more details to emerge as the launch date approaches.

content_raw: Picture Credits: Netflix After nearly 30 years in development (in various forms and statuses), legendary animation director Brad Bird’s passion project,  Ray Gunn , is finally seeing the light of day. Slated to arrive exclusively on Netflix in December 2026, the sci-fi noir detective story will be the third feature film to emerge from the multi-year deal between Netflix and Skydance Animation which will premiere at the London Film Festival.  Beyond the initial announcement back in 2024 that the movie would be part of the Skydance Animation slate coming to Netflix, there was mostly radio silence on the project—but a whole lot of hype. That all changed following Netflix’s massive showcase at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival earlier this year, where we finally got our first real look at the film. Here is our fully updated, comprehensive guide to  Ray Gunn , including the star-studded voice cast, the plot, the powerhouse creative team, brand-new runtime and rating info, and the film’s long journey to our screens. The 30-Year Journey to Netflix Ray Gunn  is the ultimate passion project. Brad Bird and Matthew Robbins originally wrote the script way back in 1996. The movie went into development at Turner Animation (Warner Bros.). For decades, it was envisioned as a 2D hand-drawn animated film but struggled to find a studio willing to back its ambitious scale and slightly more mature tone. The idea itself, however, came from a surprisingly goofy place: a misheard pop song. Speaking at Annecy Animation Film Festival , Bird revealed the spark came when he misheard the B-52s track “Planet Claire,” mistaking it for Henry Mancini’s famous “ Peter Gunn ” theme, which resulted in the mashup name “ Ray Gunn .” The project was finally revived at Skydance Animation under the leadership of John Lasseter. Originally set up at Apple TV+, the massive sci-fi epic—which reportedly carries a budget exceeding $150 million—found a new home when Skydance signed a multi-year overall pact with Netflix. It eventually transitioned from its original 2D roots into a cutting-edge 3D CG animated feature, with Cinesite assisting on the production. But animation purists, rejoice! As Bird detailed during a special Annecy panel we extensively covered,  Ray Gunn  relies entirely on pure keyframe animation. There is absolutely no motion capture used in the film.
